newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castor down on higher supply, poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian castor down on higher supply, poor demand.

text.p: Indian castorseed June delivery dropped to 1,114/1,115 rupees per quintal from 1,122 rupees on the back of renewed speculative selling on Friday, traders said.
"Higher arrivals of castorseed in producing centres and sluggish overseas buying dragged prices lower," one trader said.
Traders said the Bombay Oil Exchange opened trading in the castorseed September delivery but no deals had been done due to poor interest from market participants.

"Earlier the volume of trading in the castorseed forward deliveries was higher due to weekly clearing system but now exchange authorities have implemented daily clearing system which has depressed," one trader said.
Groundnut oil moved up to 361/362 rupees from 358 per 10 kg on renewed seasonal buying at the reduced level, traders said.
"Prices may come down again given the rising summer crop arrivals at the producing centres," one trader said.
Imported palm-oil also bounced back 2/3 rupees to 287/288 rupees per 10 kg on demand and on reports of a recovery in world markets, traders said.
"The rise in the palm-oil prices in the local market may prove shortlived looking at the increased arrivals of imported oil at the Bombay port," a trader said.
In Rajkot, spot groundnut oil was quoted 5 rupees higher at 555/560 rupees per 15 kg.
